units.name: Lesson 26 - Could, couldn't and be able to

examples.easy: The car crashed into a tree.
examples.normal: The car crashed while the driver was talking to a woman.
examples.hard: The plane crashed shortly after take-off, but luckily most of the passengers survived.

examples.easy: I looked at the shop window.
examples.normal: While I was looking in the shop window, I saw a dress.
examples.hard: Before Christmas, the shop windows in the city centre are full of lights and colourful decorations.

examples.easy: He was working in the garage.
examples.normal: I saw him when he was working in the garage.
examples.hard: We don't keep the car in our garage, because it is full of old furniture and boxes.

examples.normal: I met her in the street. She was wearing a fur coat.
examples.hard: Many people no longer buy real fur coats because they think it is cruel to animals.

examples.normal: The hotel room has a small safe for passports and money.
examples.hard: The thief opened the safe in the bank just as the police arrived, so he was caught immediately.

units.name: Lesson 32 - Past events, one/ones and objects

examples.easy: She fell asleep on the sofa.
examples.normal: She fell asleep while she was watching a romantic film.
examples.hard: I was so tired after the flight that I fell asleep as soon as I sat in the taxi.

examples.normal: Jim fell off the ladder while he was painting the ceiling.
examples.hard: Always ask someone to hold the ladder when you change a light bulb in a high room.

examples.normal: There is a big crack in the ceiling of our bedroom.
examples.hard: The rooms in old buildings often have very high ceilings, which makes them hard to heat in winter.

examples.normal: Just as I fell asleep, I heard a strange noise outside.
examples.hard: It felt strange to walk through my old school again after so many years living in another country.

examples.normal: I couldn't sleep because of the noise from the street.
examples.hard: The neighbours complained about the noise, so we turned the music down and closed all the windows.

examples.normal: As I lay in the sun, a mosquito bit my arm.
examples.hard: We closed all the windows in the evening because there were so many mosquitoes near the lake.

examples.normal: Tim washed his face and put on his uniform very quickly.
examples.hard: In many schools in Uzbekistan, students have to wear a uniform from the first to the last year.

examples.easy: He ran to the bus stop.
examples.normal: He ran to the bus stop, but he missed the bus.
examples.hard: There is a bus stop right outside our house, so I can get to work in less than twenty minutes.

examples.normal: I missed the eight o'clock train and was late for work.
examples.hard: If you don't leave now, you will miss the last bus and have to pay for an expensive taxi.

examples.normal: His wife spoke to him angrily and told him to come home.
examples.hard: When the waiter brought the wrong meal for the third time, the customer stood up and left angrily.

examples.easy: John rarely goes to the theatre.
examples.normal: We rarely eat out because restaurants here are so expensive.
examples.hard: My grandparents rarely watch television, as they prefer reading newspapers and working in their garden.

examples.normal: Last night he bought two tickets for the theatre.
examples.hard: The old theatre in the city centre has been closed for repairs, but it will open again next spring.

examples.normal: The food at the hotel was terrible, so we ate in town.
examples.hard: We had a terrible journey home because of the snow, and it took us nine hours instead of four.

examples.easy: She bought a lot of groceries.
examples.normal: Last Friday she bought a lot of groceries at the supermarket.
examples.hard: Many people now order their groceries online and have them delivered straight to their door.

examples.normal: As she paid, she dropped a banknote into one of the bags.
examples.hard: The bank is printing new banknotes that are harder to copy and last longer than the old paper ones.

examples.normal: The cashier helped her while she was looking for the money.
examples.hard: The cashier at the supermarket noticed that I had paid twice and kindly gave me my money back.

examples.normal: He hit the table and broke the vase on it.
examples.hard: My grandmother's old blue vase is the most valuable thing in our flat, so nobody is allowed to touch it.

examples.normal: What were you doing while your mother was preparing breakfast?
examples.hard: It took the whole family two days to prepare all the food for my sister's wedding party.

examples.easy: Do you have a red biro?
examples.normal: Can I borrow a biro? Mine has stopped working.
examples.hard: Please fill in the form in capital letters with a black biro, not a pencil.

examples.normal: The children were drawing pictures of animals with crayons.
examples.hard: My daughter used her new crayons to draw a birthday card for her grandmother, which made her very happy.

examples.normal: Students can't use a calculator in the maths exam.
examples.hard: I always check the bill with the calculator on my phone, because restaurants sometimes make mistakes.

examples.normal: Take your anorak with you because it might rain later.
examples.hard: He wore a thick waterproof anorak on the mountain, so he stayed dry even in the heavy rain.

examples.normal: There's a chemist's at the end of this street.
examples.hard: I went to the chemist's to buy some medicine for my cold, and the pharmacist gave me useful advice.

examples.easy: I have a notepad in my bag.
examples.normal: She always keeps a small notepad and a pen in her bag.
examples.hard: During the interview, the journalist wrote down everything I said in a little notepad.

examples.easy: My wallet is in my bag.
examples.normal: I left my wallet at home, so I couldn't pay for lunch.
examples.hard: He lost his wallet on the train, but luckily someone found it and took it to the police station.

examples.easy: We buy fruit at the market.
examples.normal: My mother goes to the market every Saturday morning.
examples.hard: The market near our house has the freshest vegetables, so I have never shopped anywhere else.

examples.easy: I bought chicken at the butcher's.
examples.normal: The butcher's on our street sells very good fresh lamb.
examples.hard: I have just been to the butcher's, so we can cook meat for dinner tonight.

examples.normal: Have you ever watched a horror film alone at night?
examples.hard: I watched a horror film last night and I couldn't sleep until three in the morning.

examples.normal: The train arrives in Samarkand at half past ten.
examples.hard: My father hasn't arrived home yet, but he will be here in a few minutes.

examples.normal: Our teacher gives us a lot of homework every week.
examples.hard: The students haven't finished their homework yet, but they promise to do it before tomorrow's lesson.

examples.normal: I have borrowed three books from the library this month.
examples.hard: He borrowed some money from his brother and promised to pay it back by Friday.

examples.normal: I usually study at the city library after work.
examples.hard: Our town library has thousands of books, and you can borrow up to five at a time.

examples.normal: The secretary has already posted all the letters today.
examples.hard: Please leave your documents with the secretary, and she will give them to the manager this afternoon.

examples.normal: Has the secretary posted the invitations to our guests yet?
examples.hard: I posted the parcel on Monday, but it still hasn't arrived at my sister's house.

examples.easy: We went to Cyprus by ship.
examples.normal: The ship leaves the port early every morning.
examples.hard: Travelling by ship takes much longer than flying, but you can enjoy the sea views on the way.

examples.easy: She went to London by air.
examples.normal: Travelling by air is quick, but it is quite expensive.
examples.hard: My grandparents have never travelled by air, because they feel safer on trains and buses.

examples.easy: The children are in the garden.
examples.normal: We have planted roses and tomatoes in our garden this year.
examples.hard: In summer my family eats dinner in the garden because it is much cooler than inside the house.

examples.normal: What have you had for breakfast this morning?
examples.hard: If I don't have a good breakfast, I usually feel tired and hungry before lunch.

examples.normal: Have you typed the letters for the meeting yet?
examples.hard: I typed the whole report on my laptop, but then I forgot to save it and lost everything.

examples.normal: We clean the house together every Sunday morning.
examples.hard: I have cleaned the kitchen, so please don't leave dirty cups on the table again.

examples.normal: Let's wait here until it stops raining, then walk home.
examples.hard: It has finally stopped raining, so we can take the children to the park this afternoon.

examples.easy: He has just had a shower.
examples.normal: I usually have a shower before I go to work.
examples.hard: After the long football match, all the players had a shower and changed into clean clothes.

examples.normal: My little son fell down in the park and hurt his knee.
examples.hard: Be careful on the icy steps, because a lot of people have fallen down there this week.

examples.normal: Can I have a look at your newspaper, please?
examples.hard: I don't buy a newspaper any more, because I read all the news on my phone every morning.

examples.normal: I can't find my umbrella. Somebody has taken it.
examples.hard: I left my umbrella on the bus this morning, so I got completely wet on the way home.

examples.normal: My eyes are not very good, so I wear glasses.
examples.hard: I have looked everywhere for my glasses, and I still can't read this message without them.

examples.normal: I haven't decided which shoes to buy for the wedding.
examples.hard: After a long discussion, my parents decided to sell the old car and buy a smaller one.

examples.normal: I have forgotten her name. Can you tell me again?
examples.hard: I'm sorry I forgot your birthday, but I was so busy at work that week.

examples.normal: We want to invite our neighbours to dinner on Friday.
examples.hard: Sue is having a party tonight, and she has invited almost everyone from her office.

examples.normal: My sister buys a fashion magazine every single month.
examples.hard: I have read an interesting article about healthy food in a magazine at the dentist's.

units.name: Lesson 34 - Present perfect with since and for

examples.normal: She hasn't seen me since her birthday last month.
examples.hard: We have been friends since we were at school together, and we still meet every week.

examples.easy: They live in a small village.
examples.normal: My grandparents have lived in this village since 1972.
examples.hard: Life in the village is quieter than in the city, but there are fewer jobs for young people.

examples.normal: He hasn't visited his uncle since he was a boy.
examples.hard: When I visited Bukhara last year, I spent two whole days looking at the old buildings.

examples.easy: He has a new white shirt.
examples.normal: He has worn the same shirt since Monday. It's dirty!
examples.hard: I need to buy a new shirt for the interview, because my old one is too small now.

examples.easy: They have been away a fortnight.
examples.normal: They haven't ridden their bicycles for the last fortnight.
examples.hard: We are going on holiday for a fortnight, so a neighbour will feed our cat while we are away.

examples.normal: Have you ever ridden a motorcycle? Yes, last weekend.
examples.hard: Roy hasn't ridden his bicycle since he fell down, because he is still afraid of having another accident.

examples.normal: He has studied maths since two o'clock this afternoon.
examples.hard: My brother has always been good at maths, so he wants to become an engineer one day.

examples.normal: I haven't eaten any cheese since breakfast this morning.
examples.hard: This shop sells cheese from many different countries, but the local one is still the cheapest.

examples.normal: She isn't ready. She hasn't packed her cases yet.
examples.hard: We always pack the night before a trip, so we don't forget anything important in the morning.

examples.normal: Please don't throw rubbish in the street. Use the bin.
examples.hard: Every Tuesday the city workers collect the rubbish, so we put the bags outside on Monday night.

examples.normal: Who has emptied the bin in the kitchen today?
examples.hard: Before the flight, the security officer asked me to empty my bag and show him everything inside.

examples.easy: They have lost their car keys.
examples.normal: I have lost my phone and I can't call anyone.
examples.hard: If you lose your passport abroad, you should go to your embassy as soon as possible.

examples.easy: John has bought a new jacket.
examples.normal: It's cold outside, so put on your warm jacket.
examples.hard: I left my jacket at the restaurant last night, and luckily the waiter kept it for me.

examples.normal: Karen has finished her violin practice for today.
examples.hard: My daughter has played the violin since she was six, and now she plays in a youth orchestra.

examples.easy: She has gone to the supermarket.
examples.normal: The supermarket near my flat is open until midnight.
examples.hard: I went to the supermarket after work yesterday, but they had already sold all the fresh bread.

examples.normal: Our football team has won all its matches this year.
examples.hard: If we win the next game, we will play in the final for the first time in ten years.

examples.normal: She is a journalist and works for a sports magazine.
examples.hard: The journalist has interviewed many famous people, but she says the president was the most difficult.

examples.normal: My sister is married and has two lovely children.
examples.hard: They have been married for thirty years, and they still go for a walk together every evening.

examples.easy: We have a flat in London.
examples.normal: We have had this flat since last May.
examples.hard: Our new flat is on the fifth floor, so we can see the whole city from the balcony.

examples.easy: He has broken the world record!
examples.normal: Great! Sean has just broken the world record in swimming.
examples.hard: Nobody has broken that world record for twenty years, so everyone was shocked when she did it.

examples.normal: Adam is clever. He has already passed all his exams.
examples.hard: You have to study hard all term if you want to pass the final exam with a good mark.

examples.normal: I have recently started learning English at an evening school.
examples.hard: Prices have gone up a lot recently, so many families are spending less on clothes and holidays.

examples.easy: She has got her driving licence.
examples.normal: My mum hasn't had an accident since she got her driving licence.
examples.hard: You can't rent a car in this country without a valid driving licence and a credit card.

examples.easy: Never tell a lie to me.
examples.normal: Have you ever told a lie to your mother?
examples.hard: He told a lie about where he was last night, and now nobody in the family trusts him.

examples.normal: Have you ever ridden a motorcycle on a mountain road?
examples.hard: My uncle rode his motorcycle across three countries last summer and filmed the whole trip.

units.name: Lesson 35 - Present perfect or past simple

examples.easy: My sister sent me a telegram.
examples.normal: Have you ever got a telegram from someone in another city?
examples.hard: In the past people sent a telegram for urgent news, but today almost everyone just sends a text message.

examples.normal: He has been absent from school for two days.
examples.hard: If you are absent from work for more than three days, you need to bring a note from your doctor.

examples.normal: I haven't slept well lately because of the noisy neighbours.
examples.hard: Who has seen Tom lately? Nobody knows where he is, and he isn't answering his phone.

examples.easy: Mr Smith works in this office.
examples.normal: Mr Smith has worked in this office for five years.
examples.hard: Our office is on the tenth floor, so most of us take the lift instead of walking up the stairs.

examples.normal: Up to now she has never phoned me at work.
examples.hard: I phoned the hotel three times this morning, but nobody answered, so I sent them an email instead.

examples.easy: There was a robbery last night.
examples.normal: Has there been a robbery here recently? Yes, two.
examples.hard: The police are still looking for the men who were responsible for the bank robbery last month.

examples.easy: She is wearing a long skirt.
examples.normal: I bought a skirt last week, but I haven't worn it yet.
examples.hard: This skirt was too short for the office, so I took it back to the shop and changed it.

examples.easy: The baby has just woken up.
examples.normal: The baby went to sleep and hasn't woken up since.
examples.hard: I usually wake up at six, but on Sundays I stay in bed until at least nine o'clock.

examples.easy: What did you do at the weekend?
examples.normal: Mr Brown usually stays at home at weekends.
examples.hard: We go to the zoo nearly every weekend, because the children love watching the monkeys and the lions.

examples.normal: He hasn't had a holiday for two years.
examples.hard: Have you ever spent a lot of money on a holiday and then felt disappointed with the hotel?

examples.normal: He has been very busy since his last holiday.
examples.hard: My father is so busy at work this month that he only comes home after the children are asleep.

examples.normal: She has been ill since her last exam, poor girl.
examples.hard: When I was ill last winter, my neighbours brought me soup and medicine every single day.

examples.normal: We had an English exam on Monday, and it was easy.
examples.hard: She studied every evening for a month, so she wasn't surprised when she passed the exam with top marks.

examples.normal: The baker's on the corner sells fresh bread every morning.
examples.hard: I wasn't at the butcher's this morning, but I've been to the baker's and bought some warm bread.

examples.easy: He never comes home before midnight.
examples.normal: Mr Smith hasn't come home yet, and it's almost midnight.
examples.hard: The last bus leaves at midnight, so if you miss it, you will have to take a taxi home.

examples.normal: I'm going to the zoo tomorrow. Have you ever been there?
examples.hard: The city zoo has over two hundred kinds of animals, and the tickets are free for small children.

examples.easy: I wash the dishes after dinner.
examples.normal: Haven't you washed the dishes yet? No, I've just started.
examples.hard: In our house the person who cooks never has to wash the dishes, so I prefer to cook.

examples.normal: The children have just eaten their sandwiches and drunk their milk.
examples.hard: I usually take a sandwich and an apple to work, because the café near my office is very expensive.

examples.normal: In 1980, Mr Smith retired from the factory and moved away.
examples.hard: My aunt wants to retire early so that she can spend more time with her grandchildren in the village.

examples.easy: He works in a car factory.
examples.normal: Many people in our town work at the old textile factory.
examples.hard: When the factory closed, hundreds of workers had to look for new jobs in the capital.

examples.easy: We moved to a new city.
examples.normal: He moved to a small city and lived there for seven years.
examples.hard: We have moved three times in the last five years, so my children have changed school very often.

examples.easy: I have been there several times.
examples.normal: I have been to London several times for work.
examples.hard: I have explained this rule several times, but some students still make the same mistake in their tests.

examples.normal: Has your mother ever made an apple pie for you?
examples.hard: My grandmother's apple pie is famous in our family, but she has never told anyone her secret recipe.

examples.easy: Have you ever stayed in a hotel?
examples.normal: We stayed in a small hotel near the sea last summer.
examples.hard: The hotel was quite expensive, but the rooms were clean and the staff were very friendly and helpful.

examples.easy: I haven't swept the floor yet.
examples.normal: Please sweep the kitchen floor before the guests arrive.
examples.hard: I haven't swept the floor yet, and it is very dirty after the children's party last night.

examples.easy: The boys have broken a vase.
examples.normal: She put the flowers in a tall glass vase.
examples.hard: My grandmother's old vase fell off the shelf and broke into pieces, so she was very upset.

examples.normal: Please copy these sentences carefully into your exercise books.
examples.hard: The teacher noticed that two students had copied each other's answers, so she gave them both a low mark.

examples.easy: Tim hasn't been to the concert.
examples.normal: We are going to a rock concert on Saturday night.
examples.hard: The concert was cancelled at the last moment, because the singer suddenly became ill.

examples.easy: She has read an interesting article.
examples.normal: Bob has just found a new article about healthy food.
examples.hard: I wrote an article about tourism for the local newspaper, and many readers sent me positive comments.

examples.normal: Our neighbours are very friendly and often help us.
examples.hard: When we were on holiday, our neighbour watered the plants and checked that everything in the flat was fine.

examples.easy: I have bought a new mobile.
examples.normal: Have you chosen a new mobile yet? Not yet.
examples.hard: I left my mobile at home this morning, so I couldn't call anyone or check my messages all day.

examples.normal: Sally has been in hospital since April, but she's better now.
examples.hard: My cousin works as a nurse in a big hospital, and she often has to work at night.

examples.easy: We have been friends since childhood.
examples.normal: I spent my childhood in a small village near Fergana.
examples.hard: Some of my happiest childhood memories are of summer evenings in my grandparents' garden.

examples.easy: I have skated on the skating rink.
examples.normal: There is a new skating rink in the centre of town.
examples.hard: Every winter the city opens an outdoor skating rink, and it is always full of families at the weekend.

examples.easy: Have you ever flown in a helicopter?
examples.normal: They have flown over the mountains in a helicopter.
examples.hard: The injured climber was taken to hospital by helicopter, because the road was blocked by snow.

examples.normal: Liz has booked a trip to Morocco for next month.
examples.hard: If you want a good room in summer, you should book the hotel at least two months in advance.

examples.easy: We have just visited an exhibition.
examples.normal: Have you attended the new art exhibition at the museum?
examples.hard: The photography exhibition was so popular that the museum decided to keep it open for another month.

examples.normal: My boss wants the report on her desk by Friday.
examples.hard: I have already written the monthly report, but I still need to check the numbers before I send it.

examples.easy: Have you been to the hairdresser's?
examples.normal: She goes to the hairdresser's once a month for a haircut.
examples.hard: I went to the hairdresser's on Saturday, but they were so busy that I had to wait for an hour.

examples.normal: How much money have you spent this week on food?
examples.hard: We spent a lot of money on our holiday, so this month we have to be careful with every penny.

examples.normal: What have you studied since the beginning of this term?
examples.hard: At the end of the term all the students take an exam, and the best ones get a prize.

examples.normal: My brother is an engineer and works for a big company.
examples.hard: She studied for five years to become an engineer, and now she designs bridges and roads.

examples.easy: They are nurses in a hospital.
examples.normal: The nurse checked my temperature and gave me some medicine.
examples.hard: Nurses often work long hours at night, but most of them say they really love helping people.

examples.normal: The shop assistant helped me find a jacket in my size.
examples.hard: My first job was as a shop assistant in a bookshop, and I learnt a lot about talking to customers.

examples.normal: The waiter brought our food very quickly and smiled a lot.
examples.hard: He worked as a waiter during his summer holidays to save money for his university studies.

examples.normal: Having a hobby helps people relax after a busy day.
examples.hard: Hobbies are very important in our life, because they help us enjoy our free time and forget about stress.

examples.normal: I give my best drawings to my friends as a gift.
examples.hard: She spends all her free time drawing pictures, and she wants to become a professional artist one day.

examples.normal: She won first prize in the school drawing competition.
examples.hard: The first prize was a trip to London, so hundreds of people took part in the competition.

examples.normal: There is a singing competition at our school every spring.
examples.hard: More than fifty students took part in the competition, so the judges needed three hours to choose the winner.

units.name: Lesson 37 - Rules: must and have to

examples.normal: It is necessary to show your passport at the airport.
examples.hard: We use 'must' when the speaker thinks it is necessary or important to do something right now.

examples.normal: In football, a rule says players can't use their hands.
examples.hard: Every club has its own rules, and members who break them more than once may have to leave.

examples.easy: Smoking here is against the law.
examples.normal: In many countries the law says you must wear a seatbelt.
examples.hard: In some countries shops have to close on Sundays, because the law does not allow them to open.

examples.normal: My father stopped smoking ten years ago and feels much better.
examples.hard: You mustn't smoke inside the building, but there is a special area outside near the car park.

examples.normal: In Britain people don't have to carry a passport with them.
examples.hard: You have to show your passport and your ticket at the airport before you can get on the plane.

examples.easy: You must work hard to succeed.
examples.normal: She succeeded in passing her driving test on the first try.
examples.hard: If you really want to succeed in business, you have to be patient and learn from every mistake you make.

examples.normal: You mustn't disturb other players during the game.
examples.hard: I'm sorry to disturb you so late, but I have an urgent question about tomorrow's meeting.

examples.easy: Please be silent in the library.
examples.normal: You don't have to be silent, but please don't shout.
examples.hard: The whole room went silent when the teacher walked in with the results of the final exam.

examples.normal: Drivers of large vehicles have to wait for the guard.
examples.hard: Large vehicles are not allowed in the city centre during the day, because the streets are very narrow.

examples.easy: Be careful when you cross the road.
examples.normal: Small children mustn't cross the busy street on their own.
examples.hard: Always look left and right before you cross the road, even when the light is green for you.

examples.normal: Please don't make a noise. The baby is sleeping.
examples.hard: The neighbours made a lot of noise until two in the morning, so nobody in our building could sleep.

examples.easy: Put the books on the shelf.
examples.normal: You don't have to put the books back on the shelves.
examples.hard: The top shelf in our kitchen is so high that I have to stand on a chair to reach it.

examples.easy: We swim in the swimming pool.
examples.normal: You mustn't eat or drink by the swimming pool.
examples.hard: Our hotel had a large outdoor swimming pool, so the children spent every afternoon in the water.

examples.easy: He has a job interview tomorrow.
examples.normal: Does your brother have to go to a job interview tomorrow?
examples.hard: Before a job interview, it is a good idea to read about the company and prepare some questions.

examples.easy: My father has to wear a tie.
examples.normal: My father has to wear a tie at work every day.
examples.hard: In many offices men don't have to wear a tie any more, except for very important meetings.

examples.easy: I have an appointment at three.
examples.normal: I have to leave soon because I have an appointment.
examples.hard: If you can't come to your appointment, please phone the clinic at least one day before.

examples.normal: My deskmate has to visit the dentist because of toothache.
examples.hard: Most people are a little nervous before they visit the dentist, even when nothing is wrong with their teeth.

examples.normal: Daniel has to be on time because his teacher is strict.
examples.hard: My parents were quite strict when I was young, so I always had to be home before nine o'clock.

examples.easy: The rent is very high here.
examples.normal: My aunt has to find a job. She can't pay her rent.
examples.hard: Rents in the city centre have gone up a lot, so many young people have moved to the suburbs.

examples.normal: Do students have to wear a uniform in your country?
examples.hard: All the nurses in this hospital have to wear a blue uniform, but the doctors can wear their own clothes.

examples.easy: You need permission to go out.
examples.normal: Our father won't give us permission to go out tonight.
examples.hard: You must ask for permission before you take any photos inside the museum.

examples.normal: Evie's washing machine is broken, so she washes everything by hand.
examples.hard: We bought a new washing machine last month, and it uses much less water and electricity than the old one.

examples.normal: Passengers have to wear a seatbelt in case of an accident.
examples.hard: In this country everyone in the car has to wear a seatbelt, and the police often check this.

examples.normal: My father has to pay the electric bill. The deadline is today.
examples.hard: I have to finish this project by Friday, but I don't think I can meet the deadline without some help.

examples.normal: I couldn't sleep last night because of a bad toothache.
examples.hard: If you have toothache for more than a day or two, you really should make an appointment with a dentist.

units.name: Lesson 38 - Duties, antiques and Bruce Lee

examples.easy: I have to feed my dog.
examples.normal: Sue has to feed her fish every morning before school.
examples.hard: While my neighbours are on holiday, I have to feed their cat and water their plants every day.

examples.easy: Leo has to take out the trash.
examples.normal: Whose turn is it to take out the trash tonight?
examples.hard: In our family everyone has a job: I wash the dishes and my brother has to take out the trash.

collocations: take out the trash every day
forget to take out the trash

examples.normal: Sarah is studying literature, so she reads a lot of books.
examples.hard: English literature is my favourite subject, because the stories help me understand how people lived in the past.

examples.normal: At the end of the course all the students take a test.
examples.hard: The cooking course lasts six weeks, and at the end every student has to prepare a three-course dinner.

examples.normal: In tennis you have to hit the ball over the net.
examples.hard: In volleyball, players must not touch the net, or the other team gets a point.

examples.easy: You have to change at Bristol.
examples.normal: This train doesn't go to London, so you have to change trains.
examples.hard: There is no direct bus to the airport, so you have to change at the central station.

examples.normal: You can't park your car here for nothing. You have to pay.
examples.hard: It is very difficult to park in the city centre, so most people come to work by metro.

examples.normal: Paul is in a hurry. He's meeting somebody in five minutes.
examples.hard: I left home in a hurry this morning and forgot my phone, my keys and my lunch on the table.

examples.normal: Jonathan Witney has an antiques shop in an old town.
examples.hard: My uncle collects antiques, and his house is full of old clocks, chairs and paintings from different countries.

examples.normal: His grandmother's clock is old, but it is not expensive.
examples.hard: The big clock in the hall has belonged to our family for a hundred years, and it still works.

examples.normal: Is your favourite old object nice, expensive or beautiful?
examples.hard: The antique table was too expensive for us, so we bought a modern one that looks almost the same.

examples.normal: Are the books and the clock for sale? No, they aren't.
examples.hard: Our neighbours' house has been for sale for months, but nobody wants to pay the price they are asking.

examples.normal: There is an antiques auction at the city hall on Saturday.
examples.hard: The old painting was sold at auction for much more money than anyone had expected.

examples.easy: You can bid for the clock.
examples.normal: You have five hundred pounds. Bid for the objects you want.
examples.hard: Two collectors bid against each other for the old clock, and the price went up very quickly.

examples.normal: Bruce Lee's father was a famous Chinese opera singer.
examples.hard: The town is famous for its beautiful old mosques, and thousands of tourists visit it every year.

examples.normal: Bruce Lee was born in San Francisco on November 27.
examples.hard: My grandfather was born in a small village, but he moved to Tashkent when he was only fifteen.

examples.normal: In Hong Kong Lee Jun Fan became a child movie star.
examples.hard: Many young actors dream of becoming movie stars, but only a few of them ever become really famous.

examples.normal: Bruce Lee opened his own very successful martial arts school.
examples.hard: My son started doing martial arts last year, and now he is calmer and more confident at school.

examples.normal: As a teenager he started getting into trouble at school.
examples.hard: If you don't do your homework on time, you will get into trouble with the teacher again.

examples.easy: He was in a street fight.
examples.normal: He often got into fights, so his parents were worried.
examples.hard: The police stopped the fight outside the stadium, but two young men had to go to hospital.

examples.normal: His parents worried, so they sent him back to America.
examples.hard: My mother always worries when I drive at night, so I message her when I get home.

examples.normal: The TV programme was very successful in America.
examples.hard: After years of hard work, she opened a successful restaurant that now has branches in three cities.

examples.normal: He began working on the TV series The Green Hornet.
examples.hard: The series was so popular that the channel decided to make a second season the following year.

examples.normal: He was taking some medicine for a bad headache.
examples.hard: I usually get a headache when I spend too many hours in front of the computer without a break.

examples.normal: He had one funeral in Hong Kong and another in America.
examples.hard: Thousands of fans came to the funeral, and many of them were crying for their famous hero.

units.name: Lesson 39 - The lion and the rabbit

examples.normal: The other animals were afraid that the lion would kill them.
examples.hard: My little sister is afraid of the dark, so we always leave a small light on in her room.

examples.normal: The plan sounded good to the lion, so he agreed.
examples.hard: After a long discussion, everyone at the meeting agreed that we needed more time to finish the project.

examples.normal: She didn't do her homework, so her father is angry.
examples.hard: The passengers got angry when the airline told them that the flight was delayed for the third time.

examples.normal: The bus always arrives at the corner of my street at four.
examples.hard: The lion was angry because the rabbit arrived very late, but the clever rabbit had a good story ready.

examples.normal: The man with the sword attacked the other man first.
examples.hard: Without waiting another moment, the lion jumped into the well to attack the other lion.

examples.easy: Look at the bottom of the page.
examples.normal: The bottom of my shoe has a hole in it.
examples.hard: The well was very deep, and there was cold dark water at the bottom of it.

examples.normal: The clever boy thought of a good idea to solve the problem.
examples.hard: All the animals in the forest were pleased with the rabbit's clever trick, because now they were safe.

examples.normal: A cruel lion lived in the forest and ate many animals.
examples.hard: It is cruel to keep a big dog in a tiny flat and never take it for a walk.

examples.normal: He finally crossed the finish line after five hours of running.
examples.hard: We waited at the airport for six hours, and finally the plane took off just after midnight.

examples.easy: The children hide behind the tree.
examples.normal: The other children will hide while you count to a hundred.
examples.hard: The rabbit said he was late because he had to hide from another lion in the forest.

examples.normal: Long ago, people hunted with bows and arrows.
examples.hard: The animals told the lion that if one of them came every day, he would not have to hunt.

examples.easy: There are a lot of apples.
examples.normal: Every day the lion killed and ate a lot of animals.
examples.hard: There were a lot of people at the market, so it took me an hour to buy vegetables.

examples.normal: The Canadian flag has a maple leaf in the middle of it.
examples.hard: The rabbit led the lion to an old well in the middle of the forest and told him to look.

examples.normal: I was only a few moments late for the meeting.
examples.hard: At that moment the lion saw his own face in the water and thought it was another lion.

examples.normal: She was pleased with the phone call she received.
examples.hard: The teacher was pleased with our results, because everyone in the class had passed the final exam.

examples.normal: He promised to return my key by tomorrow.
examples.hard: The animals asked the lion to promise that he would eat only one animal each day.

examples.normal: When she asked about the meeting, he replied, "At three."
examples.hard: I sent three emails to the company last week, but nobody has replied to any of them yet.

examples.normal: Put on your seatbelt in the car to be safe.
examples.hard: Keep your passport in a safe place, because it is very difficult to get a new one quickly abroad.

examples.normal: His card trick really surprised us at the party.
examples.hard: The rabbit's trick worked perfectly, because the lion believed that his own face in the water was an enemy.

examples.normal: The couple can dance quite well after only three lessons.
examples.hard: He speaks English well, but he still finds it difficult to understand people when they talk very fast.

units.name: Lesson 40 - Camping trip and the laboratory

examples.normal: Stop talking nonsense and tell us exactly what happened.
examples.hard: When the weatherman said it would rain, Paul said it was nonsense, but an hour later there was a storm.

examples.normal: I hope this bad weather doesn't spoil our picnic this afternoon.
examples.hard: Don't let one small mistake spoil your whole holiday, because there is still plenty of time to enjoy it.

examples.normal: Let's go and sit on the porch and enjoy the cool evening.
examples.hard: Paul left the raincoats on the front porch, so they got completely wet when the heavy rain started.

examples.normal: I'll head down to the shop after dinner to buy some milk.
examples.hard: When the storm started, we decided to head down the mountain and stay at the hotel we had passed.

examples.easy: Let's just make the best of it.
examples.normal: The hotel wasn't great, but we made the best of it.
examples.hard: It rained all week on holiday, but we decided to make the best of it and visited the museums.

collocations: try to make the best of it
just make the best of it

examples.easy: It will be a fun adventure!
examples.normal: Riding in the rough water was a real adventure for us.
examples.hard: Our trip across the desert was a great adventure, although the car broke down twice on the way.

examples.normal: One night, Mia approached the door to the laboratory.
examples.hard: As the plane approached the airport, the pilot told the passengers to fasten their seatbelts.

examples.normal: The girls walked down the dark stairs very carefully.
examples.hard: Read the contract carefully before you sign it, because some of the conditions are written in very small print.

examples.normal: Mia smelled strange chemicals in her father's laboratory.
examples.hard: Some cleaning products contain dangerous chemicals, so you should always keep them away from small children.

examples.easy: She created an igloo from snow.
examples.normal: What terrible thing was her father creating in the laboratory?
examples.hard: The new factory will create hundreds of jobs for young people who live in the area.

examples.easy: It sounded like an evil laugh.
examples.normal: The evil figure in the film scared us all.
examples.hard: In most fairy tales the evil character loses at the end, and the good characters live happily ever after.

examples.easy: We did an experiment in class.
examples.normal: The student did an interesting experiment in science class.
examples.hard: Standing outside the locked door, Mia wondered what crazy experiment her father was doing inside.

examples.normal: Mia was afraid that a monster was going to kill them.
examples.hard: Some farmers use chemicals to kill insects, but this can also be dangerous for birds and bees.

examples.easy: My mother works in a laboratory.
examples.normal: Mia's father always locked the door of his laboratory.
examples.hard: The university has built a modern laboratory where students can do experiments with the latest equipment.

examples.normal: The sound of their laugh filled the whole room.
examples.hard: The doll's laugh didn't sound so evil any more when Mia saw it in her father's hands.

examples.normal: The man's voice was so loud that we all heard him.
examples.hard: Suddenly she heard a loud noise from the laboratory, and she ran back to her room as fast as possible.

examples.normal: The boy became nervous when he heard the news.
examples.hard: Mia felt nervous about going into her father's laboratory, but in the end she agreed to go with Liz.

examples.normal: The crying baby made a loud noise all night.
examples.hard: The noise from the building site next door is so bad that I can't work from home any more.

examples.normal: His afternoon work project was to paint the room green.
examples.hard: Her father used the laboratory to do projects for work, but he never told her what they were.

examples.normal: My uncle was scared by what he saw in the room.
examples.hard: The strange laugh scared the girls so much that Mia shouted for help as loudly as she could.

examples.normal: The two boys were sharing a secret in the corner.
examples.hard: Her father smiled and said that Mia must have learned his secret, and then he showed her the doll.

examples.normal: My boss shouted at me because I was late for work.
examples.hard: When the lights went out, Mia shouted for help, and her father ran into the room at once.

examples.normal: The two friends smelled the roses in the garden.
examples.hard: Can you smell something burning? I think you have left the cake in the oven for too long.

examples.normal: The way he treated his classmate was really terrible.
examples.hard: Mia told her friend that the night before had been terrible, and she didn't want to go back.

examples.normal: Business was worse this month than last month.
examples.hard: The second laugh was even worse than the first one, and the girls were sure there was a monster downstairs.
